title: A Silver Lining Or A Shovel?
text:
A Silver Lining Or A Shovel?

Louis-Vincent Gave

Gavekal Research | 3 Nov 2026

In recent meetings with North American clients, the first question clients asked is whether bond yields in the US have risen enough to buy US treasuries (answer: most likely “yes”, at least in the short term, see Reasons To Start Buying Bonds and Why Bonds Respond To The Fed, Not To Inflation). And almost invariably, the second question has been: who are the mugs that will end up holding the bag on the now rapidly evolving French debt crisis? (answer: the European Central Bank and European insurance companies). These divergent perceptions underline an uncomfortable fact: as things stand, and for many investors, France has now become “uninvestible”; or at the very least too much of a career risk for most portfolio managers. After all, if France was to end up defaulting on its debt, or collapsing into some kind of civil disorder, portfolio managers would be blamed for failing to foresee an event even pre-announced on the cover of The Economist… not once but on an almost annual basis over the past decade.
